principles: Preserve managed asset write semantics; diagnostics must explain behavior rather than silently changing it.
Make root information machine-readable first, then render the same facts for humans.
Keep wrapper-root support explicit and covered by a regression fixture.
Avoid widening this story into unrelated gitRoot execution or external asset synchronization.
drivers: ClawCreek-style wrapper roots have metadataRoot and gitRoot split, so relative paths are ambiguous without root context.
Existing callers may depend on relPath/applied values remaining relative strings.
High-risk root diagnostics should not claim gate or authority facts beyond managed asset check scope.

options.name: A: Add metadataRoot/assetRoot/gitRoot diagnostics while preserving relPath semantics
pros: Closes the observed confusion without moving files.
Gives JSON consumers stable machine-readable root context.
Low compatibility risk because existing path fields remain unchanged.
cons: Requires callers to read a few new fields for full context.
Does not automatically repair existing external project drift.

options.name: B: Change managed asset check to operate from resolved gitRoot
pros: Makes .gitignore appear to target the git repository in wrapper-root projects.
Could reduce surprise for users who expect gitRoot to own all repo files.
cons: Breaks current global-thin metadata-root ownership model.
Could write Lattice host assets into projects that intentionally keep metadata outside gitRoot.

options.name: C: Only add a prose warning in check text output
cons: JSON consumers remain blind to the root split.
Regression tests would have to scrape prose instead of checking structured facts.
The same ambiguity would recur in rollout or future UI surfaces.

chosen: A: Add metadataRoot/assetRoot/gitRoot diagnostics while preserving relPath semantics
rationale: Option A directly fixes the user-visible ambiguity while preserving current file placement and backward-compatible relative path fields.

preMortem.scenario: JSON output adds root fields but text output still hides them on drift
preMortem.trigger: Renderer only prints root context when check passes or only in manifest line.
preMortem.consequence: Users still run check --apply without knowing which root will be modified.
preMortem.mitigation: Render root context immediately after the summary for both OK and DRIFT states.

preMortem.scenario: Implementation accidentally writes managed assets into gitRoot
preMortem.trigger: Reusing resolveProjectGitRoot for write paths instead of diagnostics only.
preMortem.consequence: Global-thin wrapper-root projects receive unexpected files under the material repo.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep applyDefinition/root calls unchanged and add tests asserting relPath semantics remain metadata-root based.

preMortem.scenario: Wrapper-root regression is too synthetic to catch the ClawCreek confusion
preMortem.trigger: Test uses metadataRoot == gitRoot or checks only direct function output without configured gitRoot.
preMortem.consequence: The exact split-root ambiguity can regress unnoticed.
preMortem.mitigation: Build a fixture with non-git metadata root plus configured gitRoot subdir and assert metadataRoot/assetRoot differ from gitRoot.
